claims.text: The equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni baseline is a single-phase FCC alloy after the standardized thermomechanical process.
Mn is a costly constituent whose reduction or replacement can improve alloy cost.
Reducing Mn content or substituting Mn changes local atomic interactions.
The compositional change shifts local energy barriers for dislocation motion.
The shifted energy barriers cause a transition from screw-dominated to edge-dominated dislocation activity.
The equiatomic baseline is implicitly screw-dislocation dominated relative to the proposed modified alloys.
A shift toward edge-dislocation activity modifies yield strength.
A shift toward edge-dislocation activity modifies strain-hardening behavior.
Mn-reduced or Mn-substituted alloys will have a higher proportion of edge dislocations than the equiatomic baseline.
Increasing the level of Mn reduction or substitution will produce a dose-dependent change in dislocation character.
The dose-dependent change in dislocation character will correlate with changes in yield stress and strain-hardening rate.
Differences in dislocation nucleation and motion are most active during the incipient stages of plastic deformation.
The proposed mechanism applies to single-phase FCC high-entropy alloys under matched processing and within the tested temperature and strain-rate range.
Short-range order and other microstructural factors may confound the relationship between elemental substitution and dislocation character.
